purpose: Make the next unsupported_scan_motion diagnosable on its first occurrence. The fault is intermittent -- one full-area run hit it on track 5, the next completed all ten tracks -- so waiting for it is the only honest option, and the recorder is what makes that wait productive.
why_not_a_side_channel: An earlier attempt recorded the same quantities from a separate ROS node subscribing to /joint_states at 100 Hz. It twice disturbed the system it was measuring: once starving the operator's 0.5 s chassis-HOLD freshness window during route planning, once causing STALE_OR_UNREADY_LOCALIZATION on track 1. Data taken that way is not trustworthy. The plugin already computes every quantity involved, so the recording belongs inside it.

design.ring: fixed-capacity POD array (agv_linescan/flight_recorder.hpp). Recording a step is an assignment into a preallocated slot; no allocation and no file access on the physics thread.
design.bounds: trimmed by simulated time span AND capped by sample count. The count bounds memory; the span keeps the window the same duration if max_step_size ever changes, so 2000 samples are never silently reinterpreted as 2 s.
design.memory: 3472 bytes per sample with contact evidence; the normal 2001-sample two-second window is about 6.63 MiB and the 4000-sample hard capacity is 13.24 MiB
design.dump: on rejection the ring is copied synchronously and queued to one FIFO diagnostic writer shared by flight dumps and events; no diagnostic file is written on the physics thread. The writer updates diagnostic_status.json atomically after every completed job and drains on a graceful shutdown.
design.window_meaning: the record ends at the rejected step. It is the two seconds BEFORE the fault, deliberately: nothing is delayed to collect data after it.

per_sample_fields: four drive shaft rates and their contact-speed conversion
per-wheel fit residual, not only the maximum
body pose and body velocity differentiated from the previous step
encoder polarity, motion state, capture active
each guard result separately: speed, lateral, yaw, residual, data validity, polarity
bounded per-wheel contact manifolds: world point, normal, depth, force magnitude and collision identity

what_the_fields_separate.single bad encoder: one wheel residual far above the other three
what_the_fields_separate.whole-vehicle slip: four wheel residuals mutually consistent but disagreeing with the differentiated body velocity
what_the_fields_separate.losing contact: a suspension position extending while the corresponding wheel contact count reaches zero
what_the_fields_separate.solver or state-read glitch: a joint value jumping for exactly one step, now correlated with contact count, normal, depth and force on that same step
what_the_fields_separate.limitation: Contact evidence is available from recorder v2 onward. The archived natural fault is v1, so the internal-edge mechanism remains unproven until a natural recurrence.

statistics_instead_of_writes.why: writing a sample every time the residual passes half the gate would become heavy I/O if it ever runs near that level
statistics_instead_of_writes.kept_in_memory: sample count, over-half and over-limit counts, maximum, 32-bin histogram, P95/P99 from the histogram
statistics_instead_of_writes.events: one event on first crossing half the limit, then only after a cooldown; all events use the same FIFO writer so events.jsonl has one writer and preserves enqueue order
statistics_instead_of_writes.block_metadata: every captured block carries the running distribution, so normal runs answer how close to the gate the system actually operates -- a question there is currently no data for at all

dump_cap: at most max_dumps files per session; further rejections increment flight_recorder_suppressed, which is reported in the event, so a throttled run is never mistaken for one that faulted only that many times

verification.method: the residual gate is lowered to 1e-9 so rejection is certain; a recoverable scene is generated. On WSL the verifier composes the project Mesa and OptiX wrappers itself; native Linux uses the installed driver runtime.
verification.not_a_reproduction: this proves the recorder fires and is complete. It says nothing about why the real 0.0425 m/s residual occurred.

results.guard_isolation: pass flags read {data:true, lateral:true, polarity:true, residual:false, speed:true, yaw:true} -- the failing guard is named, not inferred

suspension_example.reading: front and rear moving in opposite directions, i.e. pitch, is legible directly from the record

results.stop_latency_check: below the explicit 5.0 s bound; the verifier fails nonzero if stopping or the diagnostic writer exceeds its contract
results.dump_cap: with max_dumps 3 the session wrote exactly 3 files and reported 3 further suppressed dumps

verification.negative_test: --stop-latency-limit-s 0.1 fails with exit code 1; an existing --output directory is rejected without deleting its contents

unrelated_defect_encountered: the first verification attempt used headless with linescan_backend:=render and the server segfaulted in Ogre::GL3PlusBufferInterface::_firstUpload during startup, with no project code on the stack. This is the same already-recorded failure as in gui_startup_abort.json and is not caused by this change; the verification uses the optix path the real captures use.
next: Run the normal rough-road mission with contact evidence enabled. On a natural recurrence, analyze the v2 dump; do not call the internal-edge hypothesis proven from the forced-gate verification.

frame_mismatch.problem: body velocity was a world-frame position difference while the wheel fit is in base_link. After a turnaround (yaw near pi) a normal pass would show the two with opposite signs and read as whole-vehicle slip -- the exact conclusion the field exists to support.
frame_mismatch.fix: the world displacement is rotated into base_link before being stored, and the field is named body_velocity_base_link_m_s so the frame is not left to be assumed

yaw_wrap.problem: yaw rate was a plain difference of yaw angles, which crossing +/-pi turns into a spurious spike of about 2*pi/dt, precisely during the turnaround
yaw_wrap.fix: taken from the relative rotation between the two poses instead

silent_write_loss.problem: the drain supported reporting but its only caller passed false, so a full disk or a permission error would have destroyed a rare fault record with no log at all -- the opposite of what the design claimed
silent_write_loss.fix: shutdown now reports, counts the failures, and falls back to stderr when the logger is already gone; the count is published in the statistics as flight_write_failures

verification_was_not_a_gate.problem: the verification script printed its findings and exited 0 regardless, so none of the claimed behaviour was actually enforced
verification_was_not_a_gate.fix: every check is an assertion that fails the exit code: sample count, window duration, field presence and arity, per-wheel residuals being distinct, which guard failed, statistics keys, zero write failures, the dump cap and its suppression count, and the stop latency
verification_was_not_a_gate.negative_test: run with --stop-latency-limit-s 0.1 the gate reports 'stopping took 1.84 s, beyond the 0.10 s limit' and exits 1, so the assertions demonstrably fail when they should

polarity_recorded_before_it_was_checked.problem: the encoder polarity guard runs after the sample is pushed and never set its flag, so a dump would have shown polarity passing on the step it rejected
polarity_recorded_before_it_was_checked.fix: FlightRecorder::Newest() lets that guard correct its own stored result; covered by a unit test

synchronous_event_on_the_physics_thread.problem: the near-limit event serialised and appended to events.jsonl inline, putting a file write on the physics thread at the first approach to the gate -- the moment least able to absorb a disturbance
synchronous_event_on_the_physics_thread.fix: handed to the same async writer as the dumps

not_recoverable_from_a_clean_checkout.problem: the verifier hard-coded a local home path and pointed at a scene under gitignored local_data, so it could not run on another machine and leaked a local path
not_recoverable_from_a_clean_checkout.fix: the project root is derived from the script location and the scene is generated by tools/generate_shared_scene.py unless --scene is given

domain_isolation.problem: found while running the negative test: a leftover simulator collided on the controller manager and the failure surfaced as 'the simulator did not start', which would misdirect an investigation
domain_isolation.fix: the verifier runs in its own ROS_DOMAIN_ID and GZ_PARTITION derived from its pid

review_fixes_followup_2026_09_15.single_ordered_writer: Near-limit, reset, recovery and tail events plus flight dumps are queued to one FIFO worker. Independent ofstream appenders no longer race on events.jsonl.
review_fixes_followup_2026_09_15.observable_write_failures: diagnostic_status.json is created during Configure before any event can occur, then atomically refreshed after every writer job. It contains write_failures and dropped_records, survives the already-known Gazebo shutdown fault, and makes late failures externally checkable.
review_fixes_followup_2026_09_15.safe_output: --output must name a nonexistent directory; the verifier never recursively deletes a caller-owned directory.
review_fixes_followup_2026_09_15.wsl_launch: WSL detection automatically composes with_mesa_runtime.py and with_optix_runtime.sh, then reloads ROS and the workspace inside the OptiX environment. A direct invocation from a sourced workspace completed.
review_fixes_followup_2026_09_15.strict_cap_gate: verification now requires exactly max_dumps files and at least one reported suppression, not merely a file count below the cap.
review_fixes_followup_2026_09_15.latest_run: direct WSL invocation verified the status file before the first event, generated its own scene, wrote 3 dumps, reported 3 suppressions, parsed the ordered event log, left no temporary status file, reported zero writes/drops and stopped in 1.83 s.
review_fixes_followup_2026_09_15.non_intrusive_queue: Queue shutdown or allocation failure increments dropped_records and returns without throwing into PostUpdate; the writer catches both standard and unknown job exceptions.
review_fixes_followup_2026_09_15.status_delivery_order: /linescan/status publishes immediately while events.jsonl is persisted later by the FIFO writer. Online consumers use the message payload; disk readers wait for session completion.
review_fixes_followup_2026_09_15.temporary_cleanup: a stale diagnostic_status.json.tmp is removed before each atomic replacement and cleaned after a failed attempt

contact_evidence_2026_09_16.storage: 16 points per wheel per step, true count and truncation retained; no normal-path disk I/O
contact_evidence_2026_09_16.verification: 2001 samples / 2.000 s, all four streams available, maximum 10 points, zero truncation, position/normal/depth/force populated
contact_evidence_2026_09_16.analysis: tools/analyze_contact_edge_fault.py compares the fault step to the preceding step and maps points to the 10 cm cell boundary and internal diagonal
contact_evidence_2026_09_16.causality_boundary: the forced gate test verifies the recorder only; it is not evidence that the natural fault came from an internal edge
